summary: Proposes an extensible monitoring framework for RTP that adds new RTCP Extended Report block types to report media quality metrics. It recommends that a new XR block carry a single metric or a small related group. It gives guidelines for those who define such blocks. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Video calls need a report card on how well things went. This memo gives rules for adding new, small, clear lines to that report card.

questions: how to define new rtcp metrics
what is an rtcp extended report block
how do i monitor rtp stream quality
subtitle: Guidelines for designing reusable RTP monitoring report blocks.

tldr.problem: RTP applications need to monitor media quality, but many possible metrics could lead to incompatible, application-specific monitoring blocks that hurt interoperability.
tldr.mechanism: Proposes guidelines for defining RTCP Extended Report (XR) blocks that carry single metrics, are reusable across applications, and correlate with non-RTP data using RTCP SDES.
tldr.outcome: Enables simpler, more interoperable monitoring by letting applications mix and match small, focused metrics blocks rather than large monolithic ones.

today: RFC 6792 is an Informational memo from 2012. It sets guidelines that others building RTCP XR monitoring blocks are expected to follow. It has not been obsoleted or updated by later RFCs.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) carries audio and video over IP networks. To manage quality, applications need to measure and report on how well the transmission went: did packets arrive, how much delay occurred, did data get corrupted. The RTP Control Protocol (RTCP) provides this feedback.

This memo addresses a design problem: RTCP can be extended with new Extended Report (XR) blocks to carry custom metrics, but if every application designs its own large block with many metrics, the system becomes fragmented and interoperability suffers. The solution is to design small, focused metrics blocks that single concerns and can be reused across multiple applications.
sections.eli5: Different video apps might want different quality measurements. Instead of each app inventing its own report, this memo says: make small, reusable report lines that many apps can share.

sections.title: Key Concepts
sections.content:
The memo defines several categories of metrics. Transport-level metrics measure network impairments like packet loss, delay, and jitter that affect any RTP stream. Application-level metrics measure how well the application itself performs from a user's perspective, such as voice or video quality. End-system metrics measure how a device absorbs network impairments, such as through buffering or error correction.

Metrics also vary by how they are measured: direct metrics can be calculated from packets directly, interval metrics measure within a reporting window, and cumulative metrics accumulate over the entire session.
sections.eli5: Some measurements are about the network (did packets arrive?), some are about what the user sees (does the video look good?), and some are about what the device does to fix problems (did we buffer and recover?).

sections.title: The RTP Monitoring Framework
sections.content:
The framework has two main parts: a monitor (a component that collects metrics) and RTP Metrics Blocks (the data format for reporting). Monitors can live in the sender (to know what it sent), in the receiver (to know what it got), in an intermediate system like a mixer, or in a third-party device watching the network.

The collected metrics are reported in RTCP XR blocks. The monitor may also export metrics to an external management system using non-RTP protocols like SNMP or SIP.
sections.eli5: Something measures quality (the monitor), puts the measurements into report blocks, and those get sent back through RTCP or to a management system that tracks the call.

sections.title: Design Guidelines for Metrics Blocks
sections.content:
The memo gives four key design principles. First, use a single metric per block or a small set of closely related metrics. This lets applications pick and mix the blocks they need rather than forcing them to implement or ignore a large monolithic block. Second, include the payload type when a metric depends on knowing the media codec in use.

Third, use RTCP SDES to correlate XRs with non-RTP data. When RTCP reports are sent to a management system via a non-RTP protocol like SIP, the SDES (Source Description) item can carry a call identifier or other correlation information that ties the RTCP report to the non-RTP session.

Fourth, reduce measurement information duplication. When multiple metrics blocks in one RTCP packet report on the same stream for the same interval, use the Measurement Information Block to carry common data once rather than repeating it in each metrics block.
sections.eli5: Make metrics blocks small and reusable. Tell the block what kind of media it measures. Use extra fields to tie reports to the call record. Don't repeat the same measurement info across multiple blocks.

sections.title: Applicability to Network Topologies
sections.content:
The memo addresses how RTCP XR monitoring applies to different network topologies. In simple point-to-point calls, monitoring is straightforward. Translators (intermediate systems that forward packets between groups) can measure and report metrics on the streams they forward, allocating their own synchronization source (SSRC) to identify their monitoring reports.

In Multipoint Control Units (MCUs) that mix or switch media streams, RTCP reporting becomes more complex. A participant may send media to the MCU, but if the MCU does not select that stream for forwarding, the original sender will not receive RTCP reports about its stream, even though the stream may have been received correctly.
sections.eli5: Simple calls are easy to monitor. When a mixer or switch is involved, the rules get more complicated because different parts of the network see different streams.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
RTCP monitoring reports may carry sensitive information about network and application performance. If these reports are forwarded through the network by other systems, they could be exposed to malicious parties. The RFC recommends that monitoring reports be secured to the same degree as the RTP flows they measure, using encryption if needed.

The RFC also notes that other RTCP XR systems should already provide similar security properties, so RTCP XR monitoring does not introduce fundamentally new security risks.
sections.eli5: Quality reports might reveal information about calls, so they should be protected as carefully as the call data itself.

items.title: Single metric per block
items.text: Let applications mix and match what they need.

items.title: Use SDES for correlation
items.text: Tie RTCP reports to non-RTP data.
